content.text: "Research is essential. It is the lifeline of modern medicine. Incorporating research in the early years in medical school is pivotal in triggering the young minds of future physicians. This is what SRF strives to do. It is imperative to get involved in research as early as possible in medical school. That is the only way one will survive in academic medicine of the 21st century", said Dr Babar Hasan, SRF Faculty Advisor and Associate Professor, Department of Paediatrics and Child Health.

The first iteration of this event was established in 2010 with the goal of promoting the pursuit of scientific and medical research and providing students with a platform for presenting the research projects they have completed. It is the only research conference at AKU which is open exclusively to submissions from enrolled students. Thus, for many participants, it is their very first time taking part in a research conference and their first valuable real-world experience in presenting research.

"As students scramble to balance theory, clinicals and social life in medical school, it is easy to overlook the importance of research in undergraduate education. It then becomes all the more important to mentor students, igniting in them a passion for research and innovation, and a habit of asking questions" said Marvi Tariq, a final year MBBS student and Co-convener of the SRF.

An admirably large number of abstracts were received for this year's conference from which ten submissions were selected for oral presentations and fifteen for poster presentations, after careful deliberation by the SRF's core conference team.

The proceedings commenced with a recitation from the Holy Quran followed by opening remarks by the SRF Faculty Advisor, Dr. Babar Hasan. With the event underway, ten participants delivered oral presentations in the auditorium while fifteen candidates presented their posters at the poolside. Each presentation was carefully evaluated and constructively critiqued by a panel of experienced judges who additionally advised the participants on further improvements that they could make to their projects and presentation skills.

This year's participants were judged by an esteemed panel of judges including: Dr Ali Sarwar Zuberi, Assistant Professor, Department of Medicine; Dr. Masood Kadir, Associate Professor, Department of Community Health Sciences; Dr. Najia Ghanchi, Department of Pathology and Microbiology for oral presentations. Dr. Asad Ali, Associate Professor, Department of Pediatrics and Child Health, Dr Babar Hasan, Associate Professor, Department of Paediatrics and Child Health; and Dr. Ambreen Sonawalla, AKU Class of 2015, made up the panel for poster presentations.

Distinguished public health researcher, Dr. Anita Zaidi, an AKU alumna of the Class of 1988 and Director of the Diarrheal and Enteric Disease Programme at the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation delivered the keynote address at the conference. In her inspiring speech,

she talked about her journey as a researcher whilst highlighting the factors that contributed to her presently heading one of the world's foremost global health programmes as well as some of the tremendous work her organization is doing to advance the cause of public health in the world.
The conference came to a close with the distribution of awards and certificates for the winners and participants in recognition of their efforts.

In recounting their experience in organizing the event the SRF Conference Team 2016 said, "We extend our utmost gratitude to Mr Amin Lakhani for his cooperation, support and tireless efforts behind the scenes to help make the conference a success! Special thanks also to our presenters for their enthusiastic participation, and we hope that their zest for research continues!"

2nd Prize: Zoya Butt (MBBS Class of 2016) for 'Screening of Subclinical Hypothyroidism During Gestational Diabetes in Pakistani Population'

3rd Prize: shared by Aeman Muneeb (MBBS Class of 2017) for 'Quality of Life Perceptions in Adolescents Living With Social Anxiety Disorder'; and 'Alizeh Abbas  (MBBS Class of 2018) for 'Identification of Mosquito Vectors of Arboviral Infections from Aga Khan University, Karachi'
1st Prize: Lubaina Ehsan (MBBS Class of 2018) for 'Pharmacological basis for the medical use of green chilli in diarrhea'
2nd Prize: Syed Hamza Sohail (MBBS Class of 2017) for 'Comparative analysis of the anti-HCV action of sparfloxacinand ulocladium fungi derivative (Molecule-5207)'

3rd Prize: shared by Fatima Sharif (MBBS Class of 2017) for 'Trans-arterial embolization for the management of spontaneous rupture of hepatocellular carcinoma: A South Asian Experience'; and Anam Feroz (MSc Health Policy and Management Class of 2016) for 'Role of mHealth solutions in improving antenatal and postnatal care attendance in low and middle income countries: A systematic review'

content.title: Students' Health Sciences Research Conference
content.author: Hiba Khan
content.description: The Student Research Forum (SRF) at AKU organized its Fifth Annual Intra-University Students' Health Sciences Research Conference on August 26, 2016. The conference forms a core part of SRF's broader goal of promoting student-conducted research and fostering an environment of innovative thinking.
